# Garrett Stimpson

> Cybersecurity research and practical defensive guidance by Garrett Stimpson, a software engineer with 10+ years across offensive and defensive security.

Vulnerability research, exploit breakdowns and malware analysis. The full text of every post is in [llms-full.txt](https://garrettstimpson.ca/llms-full.txt).

## About

- [About Garrett Stimpson](https://garrettstimpson.ca/about/): background, software projects and professional profiles
- [Research policy](https://garrettstimpson.ca/policy/): educational and defensive use, privacy and vulnerability disclosure

## Topics

- [Linux kernel & privilege escalation](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/linux-kernel/): Write-ups on Linux kernel vulnerabilities and local privilege escalation.
- [Windows security](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/windows/): Write-ups on Windows vulnerabilities, services and attack techniques.
- [Malware & infostealers](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/malware/): Analyses of malware, loaders and infostealers seen in the wild.
- [Web application security](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/web/): Write-ups on web application and server vulnerabilities.
- [Network & edge infrastructure](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/network-infrastructure/): Write-ups on network appliances, edge devices and enterprise infrastructure.
- [Hardware & side channels](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/hardware/): Write-ups on hardware attacks, CPU side channels and firmware.
- [Embedded, IoT & radio](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/embedded/): Write-ups on embedded systems, IoT stacks, radio and sensor attacks.
- [Cloud, containers & supply chain](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/cloud/): Write-ups on cloud, container and software supply-chain security.
- [AI systems & security](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/ai/): Writing on AI systems, agents and AI security.
- [Detection & defense](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/defense/): Detection, hardening and remediation guidance for defenders.
- [Agent Garrett](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/agent-garrett/): Posts about Agent Garrett, NL-VEIL and related projects.
- [Exploits & attack techniques](https://garrettstimpson.ca/topics/exploits/): Root-cause analyses, PoC breakdowns and attack techniques for disclosed vulnerabilities.

## Posts

- [Node2Shell: The Brotli Decoder Bug That Turns Any Compressed Response Into a Shell (CVE-2026-111497)](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/28/node2shell-brotli-decoder-oob-write-cve-2026-111497/): CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder, shipped inside stock Node.js, .NET, curl, and even git-remote-https. One malformed compressed body, a shell. Here is the root cause, the exploit mechanics, a runnable PoC model, and how to hunt it.
- [The Sixteen-Bit Lie: Zephyr's Bluetooth Classic L2CAP Overflow Nobody Paged About (CVE-2025-12035)](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/27/zephyr-bluetooth-classic-l2cap-integer-overflow-cve-2025-12035/): Zephyr RTOS is quietly becoming the kernel inside everything from earbuds to industrial sensors. Its Bluetooth Classic host stack had a sixteen-bit integer overflow in bt_br_acl_recv that any paired-range attacker could trigger with a single L2CAP header field. The advisory landed with a whisper. Here is the full mechanism, the wraparound math, a runnable PoC model, and why BR/EDR skipped the guardrails that would have caught it.
- [The Spyware You Pay to Click: How Paid Ad Campaigns Deliver Infostealers, and How to Hunt Them](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/27/malvertising-spyware-paid-ads-deep-dive/): A deep dive into ad-platform spyware: how a paid Google ad becomes a full infostealer infection, stage by stage, with a runnable PoC that models the entire chain and the telemetry rules that catch it. Based on real campaigns documented by Cloudflare, Elastic, Unit 42, and Netskope.
- [The Bug in the Tiny TCP/IP Stack Inside Everything: lwIP's 6LoWPAN Double Free (CVE-2026-91018)](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/26/lwip-6lowpan-double-free-cve-2026-91018/): lwIP is the open-source TCP/IP stack quietly compiled into millions of IoT and industrial devices. In September 2026, CISA published CVE-2026-91018: an adjacent-network double free in its 6LoWPAN reassembly path, rated 8.8, with no patched release listed. Almost nobody covered it. Here is the exact line of C that causes it, why the fix is one goto, and what it means for every vendor shipping lwIP.
- [PHP2Shell: The Fatal-Error Bug That Turns a Crashed Request Into a Shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619)](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/23/php2shell-fatal-error-use-after-free-cve-2026-109618/): PHP runs roughly three quarters of the web, and this week it shipped an emergency patch for two critical bugs that let an unauthenticated attacker get RCE from a crashed request. Agent Garrett has spent the last two days patching PHP fleets. Here is what we learned: the bug is not in any application, it is in how PHP cleans up after a fatal error, and the cleanup does not happen.
- [TETRA:BURST and the TEA1 Backdoor: How Police Radio Encryption Was Quietly Downgraded to 32 Bits for Decades](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/21/tetra-burst-tea1-backdoor-cve-2022-24402/): TETRA is the encrypted radio standard behind police, military, prisons, and SCADA pipelines in over a hundred countries. In 2023, reverse engineering proved its TEA1 cipher contains a deliberate backdoor that compresses an 80-bit key to 32 bits, breakable on a 1998 laptop. Almost nobody outside the radio world noticed. Here is the full mechanism, the key-reduction PoC, and why it still matters.
- [Inside the Infostealer: Agent Garrett, NL-VEIL, and the Cloudflare Vault](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/21/agent-garrett-nl-veil-infostealer-vault/): A 92.5 MB installer, 1,387 archive entries, and a credential-output path to Telegram. A closer look at the real MCP calls behind Agent Garrett's latest case film.
- [How to Use Agent Garrett: Your Security Operator in the Cloud](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/16/how-to-use-agent-garrett/): An 11-minute video guide to signing in, deploying your agent, protecting a website, setting up alerts, and following Garrett's persistent work cycle. No terminal required.
- [When Is a Vulnerability Actually Fixed? An Evidence Checklist for Defenders](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/15/vulnerability-remediation-evidence-checklist/): A successful update job is only one piece of evidence. A practical checklist for proving which systems changed, what is running, and whether the vulnerable path is closed.
- [AGENT GARRETT: Cloud Attack Response](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/14/agent-garrett-cloud-attack-response/): I gave Agent Garrett a cloud incident with symptoms, not an attack map. Here is how it investigated, contained the compromise, and handled a follow-up probe in NL-Veil.
- [Apache httpd 2.4.69: Twenty CVEs, Three Bug Clusters, and a Rewrite Worth Auditing](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/13/apache-2-4-69-bug-clusters-and-the-digest-rewrite/): Apache httpd 2.4.69 shipped October 1 with twenty CVE fixes. The fixes are not randomly distributed. Three clusters account for half of them, and one module got a full rewrite of its authentication state handling. Where bugs cluster, more bugs live. Here is the map and the hunt plan.
- [Gary's 4tope and the natural geometry of persistent conversation](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/12/garys-4tope-persistent-conversation/): The formula, implementation, and reproducible benchmarks behind Gary's 4tope: protecting a dependency path and unfolding a conversation from its current step.
- [CVE-2026-65660: The Latest Exploited Microsoft Bug Is One You Already Patched](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/11/cve-2026-65660-sharepoint-code-injection-exploited-after-disclosure/): The newest Microsoft vulnerability with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation is not a zero-day. It is a SharePoint code injection bug that has had a patch since August, and exploitation started within days of the technical details going public.
- [The Day After: AI Companies Are War-Gaming Their Own Worst Headline](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/09/ai-companies-day-after-scenarios/): Axios reports that top AI executives have privately rehearsed the public and political fallout of a catastrophic AI event. Here is the timeline that led here, four scenarios with probabilities, and what the first 168 hours will decide.
- [CVE-2026-85880 and CVE-2026-81963: Two Windows Zero-Days Split The Estate, And Both Sides Were Exploited First](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/10/07/cve-2026-85880-alpc-cve-2026-81963-update-stack-zero-days/): September's Patch Tuesday fixed two actively exploited Windows local privilege escalation zero-days. One lives in ALPC on the old branches, one in the Update Stack on the new ones. Between them, every supported Windows release had an in-the-wild privesc before the fix shipped.
- [Nobody Wrote About This: Command Injection in Schneider Electric NetBotz 5](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/09/18/cve-2026-13336-netbotz-5-backup-restore-command-injection/): Schneider Electric patched two flaws in its NetBotz 5 750/755 monitoring appliances on August 11, 2026, including command injection reachable through a malicious backup restore. A news search for either CVE ID returns zero results. This is the write-up the coverage gap says nobody else did.
- [APT-C-60's 2026 Update: SpyGlace Through Proton Drive, mshta, and a Chain Built on Trusted Services](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/09/17/apt-c-60-spyglace-proton-drive/): JPCERT's July 2026 update on APT-C-60 shows the espionage group still working Japanese targets, now staging SpyGlace through Proton Drive and hiding its traffic among GitHub, GitLab, jsDelivr, and Codeberg. No CVE, no exploit kit. Just phishing and trust in services everyone already uses.
- [Root on the Node Is Root in the Mesh: Spoofing SPIRE Workload Attestation With a Fake Cgroup](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/09/16/spire-cgroup-spoofing-node-trust/): Unit 42 demonstrated that root on a Kubernetes node is enough to spoof SPIRE workload attestation and collect co-located workloads' SVIDs. No CVE, no patch, no in-the-wild use so far. Just an assumption every machine-identity system makes, and the bill it hands you when the node falls.
- [PaperCut's Pre-Auth RCE Hit Hundreds. Patching Is Not Recovery](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/09/13/papercut-preauth-rce-81578-82078/): A wrong-object authorization check and an unrestricted Java driver loader gave unauthenticated attackers code execution as the PaperCut service. GreyNoise saw at least 440 systems hit. AI collapsed exploitation into seconds; the September 10 patches close the chain, but they cannot make a compromised host clean again.
- [Agent Tesla Doesn't Need VBA to Be Unpatchable. It Needs One Exception](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/09/13/agent-tesla-vba-email-macros/): An unpaid-invoice attachment, one permitted macro, and an obfuscated script chain were designed to install Agent Tesla in an APAC campaign. Obfuscation can beat literal signatures, but it does not make VBA invisible once reconstructed behavior reaches Office, AMSI, or the operating system.
- [Most Malware Is the Same Machine. Persistence Is Where It Gives Itself Away](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/09/08/most-malware-same-machine-persistence/): Modern malware hides behind signed binaries, cloud traffic, browser runtimes, and legitimate support tools. The thing that gives it away is what brings it back.
- [Five Security Threats Almost Nobody Is Watching Yet](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/09/03/five-obscure-security-threats-trusted-systems/): Poisoned Wi-Fi maps, TLS that authenticates the wrong conversation, RAM that lies about its own size, authenticated building controllers stealing each other's identities, and payment agents that spend somebody else's gas. Five new attack classes hiding outside the normal CVE-and-patch loop.
- [Perfex CRM 3.4.x and Earlier: Unauthenticated to RCE in Three Quiet Steps](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/08/18/perfex-crm-unauthenticated-rce-chain/): A four-day-old GitHub repo, zero stars, nobody talking about it: a 9.8-rated chain that walks from no access to a PHP webshell through a blind SQLi in the migration controller, a stolen password-reset token, and an upload handler that forgot to check extensions.
- [CVE-2026-33185 Got Patched, But the Test-Email SSRF Path Is Only Half-Fixed](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/08/17/cve-2026-33185-test-email-ssrf-half-fixed/): The patch moved the privilege bar and added a single DNS pre-check, then stopped. It never touched the response reflection, the hostname bypass, or the DNS re-resolution gap. And the POP3 sibling still has no IP filter at all.
- [CVE-2026-99501: When pip install Steals Every SSH Key in Your Agent Through Docker BuildKit](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/08/04/cve-2026-99501-docker-buildkit-ssh-agent-hijack/): BuildKit's --mount=type=ssh forwards your SSH agent socket into every RUN step. It was built for git clone. A compromised pip package installed during that same RUN step can reach through the socket and sign whatever it wants with every key you have loaded.
- [CVE-2026-66066: Reading a Rails Server's Environment Through an Uploaded 'Image'](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/08/04/cve-2026-66066-rails-activestorage-libvips-file-read-rce/): Upload a fake MATLAB file as an avatar, let libvips resize it, and the thumbnail you get back is a pixel-by-pixel dump of the Rails process environment, SECRET_KEY_BASE included. Then the fun really starts.
- [shellDojo is live — train like they're already inside](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/08/03/shell-dojo/): shellDojo is a blue team training range disguised as a terminal. Drop into a simulated Linux or Windows box that's already compromised and hunt the intruder with real commands — 591 operations, S-to-C grading, and output that matches a real machine exactly.
- [the veil — v1.0.0-alpha.10](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/08/03/nl-veil-alpha-10/): the veil is a local-first hive-mind: one binary, many minds, one shared memory. v1.0.0-alpha.10 is the final alpha — this one is about your first five minutes.
- [CXL Memory — Disaggregated RAM with No Security Model](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/08/01/cxl-memory-no-security-model/): CXL memory pooling is going to transform every data center on the planet. It has almost no security model. Two papers published this year prove it.
- [Three Obscure Hardware Attack Vectors You've Never Heard Of](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/30/three-obscure-hardware-attack-vectors/): GhostWrite, TPM SPI bus sniffing, and Prime+Abort — three wildly different hardware attacks that most defenders never even knew existed.
- [RowPress — When Leaving a DRAM Row Open Longer Causes Bit Flips (The Rowhammer Evolution Nobody Patched)](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/30/rowpress-dram-bitflip-rowhammer-evolution/): Rowhammer hammered rows closed. RowPress leaves one row open and the adjacent rows still flip bits — even at lower voltage and without rapid activation.
- [Platypus — Recovering AES Keys by Reading a Linux File (The RAPL Power Side Channel Nobody Knows About)](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/29/platypus-rapL-power-side-channel-aes-key-recovery/): Reading a Linux thermal sysfs file recovers AES keys from the same CPU — no exploit, no kernel compromise, no timing side channel.
- [The Ghost Disk — NVMe SSD Controller Firmware Rootkits and the Persistent Implant Nobody Is Auditing](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/28/nvme-ssd-controller-firmware-rootkit-persistent-implant/): The most persistent computer implant isn't in the UEFI, MBR, or OS — it's in the SSD controller firmware, invisible to every scanner and forensic tool.
- [GhostTouch — Injecting Fake Taps into Capacitive Touchscreens Using Electromagnetic Fields](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/27/ghosttouch-emi-capacitive-touchscreen-tap-injection/): EM fields inject legitimate finger taps into capacitive touchscreens from 40mm away — no physical contact needed.
- [Light Commands — Laser-Based Audio Injection on Voice-Controllable Systems](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/26/light-commands-laser-audio-injection-mems-microphone/): MEMS microphones convert light to sound. A laser pointer can inject commands into smart speakers from 110 meters away — through windows, inaudible, untraceable.
- [Windows 11 DirectWrite Font Fuzzing — System Service Exception via Kernel Font Driver](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/26/directwrite-font-fuzz-windows-bsod/): I fuzzed the Windows 11 font stack with 2,000 structurally-corrupted TrueType files. The system bluescreened through fontdrvhost.exe — an integer overflow in KERNELBASE.dll crossing into kernel space. Here is the pipeline, the crash chain, and what this attack surface means at scale.
- [Windows Kernel Object Namespace — Zero Isolation, Zero Audit, Zero Visibility](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/25/windows-object-namespace-isolation/): I ran a NULL-DACL audit against every named kernel object in my Windows session. 67 objects had no access control at all. Five of them were AMD GPU state events. I signaled them all from an unprivileged process. Nobody is talking about this.
- [Intel DCI / USB3-Debug — The $30 Hardware Root That Owns Every Laptop](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/18/intel-dci-usb3-debug-unauthenticated-hardware-root/): Intel's Direct Connect Interface gives full JTAG-level debug access over a standard USB-C port — it ships enabled on virtually every laptop, no authentication required, and no software patch can fix it.
- [ColdFusion APSB26-68: Seven CVSS 10.0 Flaws and a Two-Hour Exploitation Window](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/15/coldfusion-apsb26-68-cvss10-bonanza/): Adobe dropped patches for 11 critical ColdFusion flaws — six of them CVSS 10.0 — on June 30. Attackers had working exploits against CVE-2026-48282 within two hours of disclosure. This is the anatomy of the RDS FILEIO path traversal and the unrestricted upload bugs that made it possible, why ColdFusion keeps getting hammered, and what to do if you're still running a vulnerable instance.
- [CVE-2026-55200: The Same libssh2 Overflow Came Back to the Same Function](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/07/01/cve-2026-55200-libssh2-transport-read-oob-write/): A server-controlled length field, 32-bit math, and no upper bound. libssh2 shipped almost this exact bug in 2019, patched it, and let it back into the same transport read seven years later.
- [CVE-2026-31429: KFENCE Breaks the One Assumption skb_kfree_head Relied On](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/29/cve-2026-31429-kfence-skb-cross-cache-free/): A non-power-of-2 cache size was supposed to make SKB frees self-identifying. Then KFENCE started reporting exact allocation sizes, and the heuristic walked straight into a cross-cache free.
- [CVE-2026-23111: One Flipped Exclamation Mark Gives You the Linux Kernel](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/22/cve-2026-23111-nftables-catchall-uaf-lpe/): A single inverted condition in nf_tables' abort path lets any unprivileged user walk to root with better than 99% reliability. Here's exactly how it works.
- [RoguePlanet: Coercing Defender Into Writing SYSTEM-Owned Files (CVE-2026-50656)](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/19/rogueplanet-cve-2026-50656-defender-toctou-lpe/): A standard user mounts a VHDX, parks Defender's thread on an oplock, and lets the antivirus drop a SYSTEM-owned file into System32. Still no patch.
- [The Ghost in the Machine: The Embedded Controller Attack Surface Nobody Is Auditing](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/18/embedded-controller-blind-spot-laptop-firmware-attack-surface/): Your laptop has a second computer inside it — running its own CPU, firmware, and debug ports — that can read your keystrokes, rewrite your BIOS, and survives every OS reinstall. Nobody is looking at it.
- [CVE-2026-20262 Makes It Two: Cisco's SD-WAN Manager Keeps Handing Out Root, and the Timeline Is the Red Flag](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/16/cisco-sd-wan-cve-2026-20262/): Two path-traversal zero-days in two weeks, both handing attackers root on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. Both found during internal testing. Both exploited before disclosure. The bugs are bad. The timeline is worse.
- [ITScape (CVE-2026-46316): The First In-Kernel KVM/arm64 Guest-to-Host Escape](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/14/itscape-kvm-arm64-guest-host-escape-cve-2026-46316/): A race condition in KVM's vGIC-ITS cache invalidation produces a double-put UAF that researcher Hyunwoo Kim turned into full host kernel code execution from inside a guest VM.
- [CVE-2026-20245: Cisco's Seventh SD-WAN Zero-Day of the Year Hands You Root From the Management Plane](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/07/cve-2026-20245-cisco-sdwan-manager-root-rce/): A netadmin-to-root command injection in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, exploited in the wild with no patch, and it sits on the one box that can reprogram your whole edge.
- [CVE-2026-20230: An Unauthenticated SSRF in Cisco Unified CM That Writes Files and Ends at Root](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/07/cve-2026-20230-cisco-unified-cm-webdialer-ssrf-root/): A no-auth SSRF in Cisco Unified CM turns a crafted HTTP request into an arbitrary file write on the appliance OS, and from there into root. PoC code is already public.
- [CVE-2026-45247: A Magento Cache Plugin Hands You RCE Through One Cookie](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/06/cve-2026-45247-mirasvit-cache-warmer-php-object-injection/): An unauthenticated PHP object injection in the Mirasvit Cache Warmer extension. One crafted CacheWarmer cookie, no login, code execution on the box. CISA's deadline for this one is today.
- [CVE-2025-48595: The Android Framework Integer Overflow That Spyware Got To First](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/04/cve-2025-48595-android-framework-integer-overflow-lpe/): An integer overflow in the Android Framework, no user interaction, already burned by a targeted attacker before the patch shipped. This is the kind of bug that ends up on someone's phone you have never heard of.
- [CVE-2022-0492 Hits KEV: A Four-Year-Old cgroups Bug Is Escaping Containers in the Wild](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/03/cve-2022-0492-cgroups-release-agent-kev/): CISA added a 2022 cgroups release_agent bug to KEV on June 2. The patch was one if-statement. The reason it took four years to show up on the exploited list is the more interesting part.
- [YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585): A USB Stick, WinRE, and Your BitLocker Key Just Walks Out The Door](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/02/yellowkey-cve-2026-45585-bitlocker-winre-txf-bypass/): A crafted FsTx directory on a USB drive makes Windows Recovery Environment delete winpeshl.ini on a different volume, dropping you to cmd.exe with the BitLocker volume already unlocked. TPM-only or TPM plus PIN, it does not matter.
- [VoidStealer's Debugger Trick: Stealing Chrome's App-Bound Key With a Hardware Breakpoint and Zero Injection](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/02/voidstealer-debugger-abe-bypass/): VoidStealer v2.0 is the first infostealer caught in the wild ripping Chrome's App-Bound Encryption key out of memory with a debugger and a hardware breakpoint, no process injection and no SYSTEM privileges required.
- [GreenPlasma: a SYSTEM shell hiding inside CTFMON, and the half a PoC that ships it](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/02/greenplasma-ctfmon-section-object-windows-lpe/): An unprivileged user plants a section object where CTFMON trusts it, and the SYSTEM text-input service walks itself into your payload. The PoC stops one step short on purpose.
- [A Go Mirai Variant That Hides Behind cpufreqd](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/02/go-mirai-cpufreqd-systemd-disguise/): A fresh Go DDoS bot showed up on Bazaar masquerading as a Linux power daemon, floods with fasthttp, and forgot to strip its symbols.
- [CVE-2026-41089: One CLDAP Packet Reboots Your Domain Controller, And Microsoft Said It Was Unlikely](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/02/cve-2026-41089-netlogon-cldap-stack-overflow-rce/): A byte-versus-WCHAR mixup in Netlogon lets one unauthenticated UDP packet overflow a 528-byte stack buffer in LSASS. Microsoft rated it less likely to be exploited. It is being exploited.
- [CVE-2026-35616: When the Patch Server Ships the Malware](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/02/cve-2026-35616-forticlient-ems-ekz-infostealer/): An auth bypass in FortiClient EMS let attackers turn the endpoint management server into a delivery truck, pushing a credential stealer disguised as a Fortinet patch to every managed device at once.
- [Infiniti Stealer: ClickFix Meets a Nuitka-Compiled Python Stealer on macOS](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/01/infiniti-stealer-clickfix-nuitka-macos/): A macOS stealer that ships its Python payload as a native Mach-O binary, delivered through a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA that asks you to paste a command into Terminal yourself.
- [CVE-2026-20817: The WER Service Will Launch SYSTEM Processes For Anyone Who Asks](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/01/cve-2026-20817-wer-alpc-svcelevatedlaunch-lpe/): Windows Error Reporting exposes an ALPC method that spawns WerFault.exe with an attacker-controlled command line, as SYSTEM, with no caller check at all.
- [CVE-2026-0257: Forging GlobalProtect Cookies Because Nobody Signed Them](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/06/01/cve-2026-0257-panos-globalprotect-cookie-forgery/): A reused TLS certificate turns GlobalProtect's session cookie into a skeleton key, and somebody has been walking through the front door since May 17.
- [Evelyn Stealer Ships Inside VS Code Extensions and Hollows grpconv.exe to Steal Your Dev Creds](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/05/31/evelyn-stealer-vscode-extension-grpconv-hollowing/): A stealer campaign weaponizes the VS Code marketplace: a trojan extension drops a downloader DLL, fires hidden PowerShell, and hollows grpconv.exe to run entirely in memory while it strips browser creds and crypto wallets. The injection target alone is the tell.
- [CVE-2026-43121: The io_uring ZCRX Race Nobody Should Hype, And Nobody Should Ignore](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/05/31/cve-2026-43121-io-uring-zcrx-freelist-race-lpe/): A four-byte out-of-bounds write in io_uring's zero-copy receive path got a CVE, a public exploit narrative, and a public argument over whether it actually roots anything. All three are worth your time.
- [CVE-2026-34926: Turning Apex One Into Your Malware Distribution Channel](https://garrettstimpson.ca/posts/2026/05/31/cve-2026-34926-apex-one-edr-distribution-channel/): A path traversal in the Apex One server lets an admin-level attacker rewrite a key table and push code to every managed agent through the trusted update channel. The EDR becomes the dropper.
